name: DatasetQuery
title: Dataset Query
description: Read rows back from the table an object owns: filtered by any declared column, limited, and summed only ever within one unit
whenToUse: Answer a question from figures that were stored rather than from a document: what a subject's figure was at a date, which subjects carry the most of something, how a figure moved between two dates. Filter by a value, a list of values or a range; group and sum to rank. A sum is always grouped by unit as well, because a share, an amount of money and a count are three different things and a total mixing them means nothing. Always filtered and always limited: it cannot be asked for a whole table. For what a document SAYS, read the document.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Upstream data; the filter is read from config

outputs.name: rows
outputs.description: The rows, or when summing, one row per group with its total and how many rows made it

object.title: Object
object.description: Which object's table, by its name

org.title: Organisation
org.description: Whose rows. Enforced by the database, not by this filter

of.title: Of
of.description: The id of the row whose figures to read. Leave empty to read across every row of this object in the organisation

where.title: Where
where.description: The filter, as a JSON array of { column, is }, { column, oneOf: [...] }, { column, from, to } or { column, startsWith }. A column the object does not declare is refused.

groupBy.title: Group by
groupBy.description: Columns to group by when summing, as a JSON array. The unit is always added

sum.title: Sum
sum.description: The column to add up. Leave empty to return rows rather than totals

orderBy.title: Order by
orderBy.description: The column to order rows by. Ignored when summing, which orders by the total

limit.title: At most
limit.description: How many rows to return, 1 to 1000

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: dataset
package.packageFile:
# DATASET — the table an object owns (docs/unoverse/data/objects/dataset.md). An object that
# holds many small facts read together, rather than one row read alone, declares its columns and
# the platform makes it a real table: real types, real indexes, and access the database enforces.
#
# TWO DOORS, two nodes. Rows in (DatasetRecord), rows out (DatasetQuery). Neither can create or
# alter a table: structure changes only through a migration generated from the declaration and
# approved by a person, and the role this runs as has no permission to do otherwise.
#
# THE HOST IS THE ENGINE, at loopback, as the documents package explains: a node's call must be
# https or loopback, and the engine holds what the database's address is so no node and no file
# does.
name: dataset
displayName: Dataset
description: >-
  Put rows into the table an object owns, and read them back: filtered, limited, and summed only
  within one unit
version: 0.1.0
category: storage
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Write a read's rows, replacing what the same document wrote last time
  - Read rows back filtered by any declared column, by value, by list or by range
  - Sum and rank, always grouped by unit so unlike figures are never added together
  - Every column checked against the object's own declaration, so a name is never taken from a caller

allowedHosts:
  - 127.0.0.1

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  transport: [json]

files.api/events.yaml:
- emit: rows
  value: "return (response || {}).rows || []"
- emit: total
  value: "return ((response || {}).rows || []).length"
files.api/run.yaml:
- name: rows
  method: POST
  url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/dataset/query'"
  transport: json
  body:
    object: "{{ config.object }}"
    org: "{{ config.org }}"
    of: "{{ config.of }}"
    where: >-
      return (() => { const r = config.where; return Array.isArray(r) ? r : (String(r || '').trim() ? JSON.parse(String(r)) : []); })()
    groupBy: >-
      return (() => { const r = config.groupBy; return Array.isArray(r) ? r : (String(r || '').trim() ? JSON.parse(String(r)) : []); })()
    sum: "{{ config.sum }}"
    orderBy: "{{ config.orderBy }}"
    descending: "return config.descending !== false"
    limit: "return Number(config.limit || 200)"
  timeoutMs: 30000
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: "return response.error"
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [object]
  properties:
    object:
      type: string
      title: Object
      description: Which object's table, by its name
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    org:
      type: string
      title: Organisation
      description: Whose rows. Enforced by the database, not by this filter
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    of:
      type: string
      title: Of
      description: The id of the row whose figures to read. Leave empty to read across every row of this object in the organisation
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    where:
      type: string
      title: Where
      description: >-
        The filter, as a JSON array of { column, is }, { column, oneOf: [...] },
        { column, from, to } or { column, startsWith }. A column the object does not declare is
        refused.
      default: "[]"
      "ui:field": template
    groupBy:
      type: string
      title: Group by
      description: Columns to group by when summing, as a JSON array. The unit is always added
      default: "[]"
      "ui:field": template
    sum:
      type: string
      title: Sum
      description: The column to add up. Leave empty to return rows rather than totals
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    orderBy:
      type: string
      title: Order by
      description: The column to order rows by. Ignored when summing, which orders by the total
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    descending:
      type: boolean
      title: Largest first
      default: true
    limit:
      type: number
      title: At most
      description: How many rows to return, 1 to 1000
      default: 200
"ui:order": [object, org, of, where, sum, groupBy, orderBy, descending, limit]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Upstream data; the filter is read from config
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: rows
    type: array
    description: The rows, or when summing, one row per group with its total and how many rows made it
  - name: total
    type: number
    description: How many rows came back

credentials: []

files.test.yaml:
# SAMPLE DATA, so the node can be loaded and run from the Nodes screen. It asks the question the
# table exists for: which subject carries the most of something, summed within one unit.
testData:
  config:
    object: observation
    org: example
    where: >-
      [{"column":"measure","is":"exposure"},
       {"column":"scope","is":"whole"},
       {"column":"label","is":"Alpha"}]
    sum: value
    groupBy: '["fund"]'
    descending: true
    limit: 10
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    rows: "return Array.isArray(output.rows) && output.rows.every(r => 'total' in r && 'unit' in r)"
    total: "return typeof output.total === 'number'"
